answer: Staking a refundable bond per identity stops Sybils by making each fake account cost real capital upfront. Like an anchor holding one ship, each agent locks a bond that is slashed if duplicates or fraud are found, so one person cannot cheaply run thousands of identities. An attacker must fund a separate terrace of bonds for every fake, tying up capital that cannot be reused elsewhere, and a saffron stain of linked fraud revokes the whole cluster, so the cost rises with each fake while honest agents pay only once and get their bond back.
